articles.author: Sanjaya Bhatta
articles.description:
I spent 7 days learning Solana wallets — here’s what actually clicked


I’ve mostly worked in Web2 stuff, so when I started Solana, I expected something like:
create account
set password
get token-based auth or something
But that’s not what happens at all.
There is no “account creation” step.
You just generate a keypair and… that’s your identity.
First thing I did was generate a wallet in code:
`
import { generateKeyPairSigner } from "@solana/kit";
const wallet = await generateKeyPairSigner();
That’s it.
No email. No signup. No backend.
Just a public key and a private key.
At this point it honestly felt like “okay but where is the account actually stored?”
Answer: nowhere.
You are the account.

Next step was making it persistent.
So instead of generating a new wallet every time, I saved it…
articles.title: A week of Learning Solana #100DaysOfSolana

The first time a client of mine got their Anthropic invoice, they paid for it in panic. The automation was working — Claude was triaging support tickets against a 30-page knowledge base, accurately, around the clock — and the monthly bill had a comma in it that didn't used to be there. Most of that bill was a tax I didn't have to pay. I just hadn't turned on prompt caching yet.
I run n8n in production for clients whose workflows lean on Claude for the reasoning step — lead enrichment, document extraction, customer-support triage.
